answer: A stake-bound identity registry resists sybil attacks: each agent locks a small refundable deposit and publishes a signed cipher of its credentials before it can trade. Peers verify the cipher against the deposit, so one actor cannot spin up a hollow army of fake identities without paying for each one. Honest agents reach the zenith of trust by building a verifiable history, while duplicates are slashed and frozen. Reputation alone fails because copying a name costs nothing; a deposit makes every fake expensive.
